history.summary: ISKCON (International Society for Krishna Consciousness) temple on Sarania Hill in the Ulubari area, Guwahati, dedicated to Krishna and his consort Rukmini. A stark white, marble-floored temple belonging to the Gaudiya Vaishnava movement founded by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. Daily programmes include aarti, kirtan, chanting and Bhagavad Gita discourses; the temple runs personality-development and stress-management classes and a religious souvenir shop. No entry fee; donations encouraged. CSV town 'Dispur' corrected to Guwahati. Coordinates from the temple's official listing (26.176755, 91.759195); the map geocoder matched an unrelated Krishna temple elsewhere in Guwahati.

name: ISKCON Temple, Guwahati
town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the principal city of Northeast India, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Once the seat of the ancient kingdom of Pragjyotishpura/Kamarupa, it is the region's main commercial and transport hub and a centre of Shakti worship, with Kamakhya, Umananda and Ugratara shrines.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, about 20 km away
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station, about 2-3 km away
travel.road: On Sarania Hill, Ulubari (near RG Baruah Road); reached by taxi, rickshaw or a flight of stairs from the entrance

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami and Rath Yatra attract large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM to 12:30 PM and 4:30 PM to 8:30 PM (travel sources); the temple's BACE listing shows 4:30 AM-1:00 PM and 3:30-8:30 PM - verify locally
